title: Tetris: Pajitnov (1984), the seven four-square pieces, the “Tetris effect” study, the Oxford flashback study and the 2023 crash

facts.text: Alexey Pajitnov, a Soviet computer engineer in Moscow, created Tetris in 1984.
In Tetris, falling pieces must be fitted together to fill rows.
Each Tetris piece is made of four squares, and there are seven different shapes.
A version for Nintendo’s Game Boy (1989) became the game’s most popular release.
In a Harvard sleep study (2000), many new Tetris players saw falling pieces as they fell asleep.
Patients with amnesia in that study also saw the images, though they did not recall playing.
The study helped make the name Tetris effect widely known.
In a 2009 Oxford study, people who played Tetris after viewing a distressing film had fewer flashbacks over the next week.
The researchers described the 2009 findings as preliminary.
In late 2023 a 13-year-old became the first known player to beat the original NES Tetris.
He played so far that the game froze (crashed); it had long been thought to go on forever.
